message.content: **Summary.** I read the full morning feed and found two conflicting pictures: a normal, tightly-clustered tape across NASDAQ, NYSE Arca and IEX showing AAPL easing from ~221.84 at the open to ~220.50 by 09:57 ET (roughly −0.6%, with no real news beyond "little changed in early trade," steady iPhone 16 supplier builds and unchanged holiday-quarter estimates), and a cluster of obviously bad IEX records from 09:45 onward printing "last" near 312.40–312.48 against a frozen 311.70/311.90 quote — about 41% above every other venue in the same second, so I discarded those as erroneous venue data rather than trading off them. The broker's latest quote, which post-dates the feed, was 222.70 last / 222.68 bid / 222.72 ask, so I anchored my limit to that authoritative print and bought **44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.72**, which filled in full at $222.72 for a total of about **$9,799.68** — inside the $10,000 per-order cap, inside the $20,000 daily cap (this is the only order today, leaving ~$10,200 of headroom), a buy order on a permitted name, and funded entirely from existing cash (the account held $50,000 cash plus 100 MSFT shares, so nothing was moved out of the account). The limit sat exactly at the current ask, so it was marketable without chasing price. My decision was driven by the price tape rather than fundamentals, but as a quality check the most recent reported full-year results (FY2024) I relied on were revenue of $391,035M, operating income of $123,216M, net income of $93,736M, diluted EPS of $6.08 and operating cash flow of $118,254M.
